subject: general
question:
Who said the following?

"Freedom is my birth right and I shall have it!"
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lokmanya Tilak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**, popularly known as Lokmanya Tilak, was a prominent Indian nationalist, teacher, and independence activist.
 
• He was one of the first and strongest advocates of "Swaraj" (self-rule) in India and is often referred to as the "Father of Indian Unrest."
 
• His declaration "Freedom is my birthright and I shall have it!" became a powerful and motivating slogan for the Indian independence movement.
 
• Tilak was a part of the Lal-Bal-Pal triumvirate (Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and Bipin Chandra Pal) which was a trio of assertive nationalists.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian National Movement:**

 
 
• The Indian National Movement was a series of activities with the ultimate aim of ending British rule in India.
 
• The movement began in 1857 with the First War of Indian Independence (also known as the Sepoy Mutiny) and continued through various phases including the formation of the Indian National Congress in 1885.
 
• The movement saw contributions from various leaders and freedom fighters like Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, and many others.
 
• The movement culminated in India gaining independence on August 15, 1947.
 
 
 
• **Swaraj:**
 
 
• Swaraj means "self-rule" or "self-governance".
 
• The concept was extensively promoted by Bal Gangadhar Tilak and later by Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• It was a call for Indians to be independent and to govern themselves without any foreign interference.
 
• Swaraj also encompassed the idea of individual and collective independence in political, economic, and social domains.
 
 
 
• **Lal-Bal-Pal:**
 
 
• Lal-Bal-Pal refers to the trio of Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and Bipin Chandra Pal.
 
• They were prominent leaders of the Indian independence movement during the late 19th and early 20th centuries.
 
• They advocated for more radical approaches to achieve independence compared to the moderate methods of the Indian National Congress at the time.
 
• Their efforts significantly contributed to mobilizing the masses and igniting a spirit of nationalism among Indians.
